packageRules.description: Speakeasy generates pyproject.toml, so updates change only uv.lock while the new version is within the declared range.
Speakeasy pins the dev tools (dependency-groups) exactly and writes build-system.requires, so any regular update would edit pyproject.toml and be reverted; the final rule keeps security updates.
As in continuous: manifests' toolchain and runtime constraints, workflow runners, package overrides and Go replace directives keep their hand-set versions.

prBodyNotes: `pyproject.toml` is generator-owned: Speakeasy rewrites it on every regeneration. If this PR changes `pyproject.toml`, add the same floor to `.speakeasy/gen.yaml` under `python.additionalDependencies.main (or .dev)` in this PR, or the next regeneration reverts it. A change to the lock file only survives regeneration.

packageRules.description: As in continuous: a rule above that matches every update type disables dependencies only after lookup, when Renovate knows which updates fix a vulnerability, so this rule keeps their security updates.

Operator decision 2026-11-13 (continuous-python PR 57): pylint is a generator-pinned dev-only tool and Dependabot alert 3 is dismissed as tolerable risk; OSV does not know about the dismissal. The rule matches only while GHSA-22qq-2fwx-7p67 is the one advisory fixed, so a new pylint advisory still gets its PR.
